title: Cell Biology: The Building Blocks of Life

summary.overview: Cells are the basic units of life. Their structures work together to regulate transport, store genetic information, synthesize proteins, and supply energy.
section_summaries: Cells share basic structures but differ in organization.
Eukaryotic organelles carry out specialized functions.
Plant cells have structures supporting photosynthesis, storage, and rigidity.
key_takeaways: Match each cell structure to its function.
summary.final_review: Focus on structure–function relationships rather than memorizing names in isolation.

topics.title: What makes a cell?
topics.summary: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of living organisms. The cell membrane separates the cell from its surroundings.
key_points: The cell membrane regulates the entry and exit of substances.
Prokaryotic cells do not have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.

key_terms.definition: The basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
A selectively permeable boundary that regulates movement into and out of a cell.

examples: Prokaryotic DNA is not enclosed in a membrane-bound nucleus.
relationships: Membrane selectivity supports regulation of the cell’s internal environment.

topics.title: Organelles and their jobs
topics.summary: Eukaryotic cells contain specialized structures that perform essential functions.
key_points: The nucleus contains most cellular DNA.
Mitochondria are involved in ATP production.

key_terms.definition: An organelle that contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s DNA.
An organelle involved in aerobic cellular respiration and ATP production.

relationships: Different structures divide the work of maintaining the cell.

topics.title: A closer look at plant cells
topics.summary: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts in photosynthetic tissues, and a large central vacuole.
key_points: Cell walls provide support outside the membrane.
The central vacuole supports storage and turgor pressure.

key_terms.definition: The organelle where photosynthesis occurs in plant cells.

examples: A chloroplast is a photosynthetic organelle.
relationships: The wall and vacuole contribute to plant-cell support.

flashcards.question: What is the basic unit of life?
What does the cell membrane do?
flashcards.answer: It regulates movement of substances into and out of the cell.

flashcards.question: Where is most DNA found in a eukaryotic cell?
What is a major role of mitochondria?
flashcards.answer: ATP production through aerobic cellular respiration.

flashcards.question: Where does photosynthesis take place in plant cells?
What does selectively permeable mean?
flashcards.answer: Some substances can cross the membrane more easily than others.

flashcards.question: How do plant cell walls differ from cell membranes?
flashcards.answer: Cell walls provide rigid support outside the cell membrane; membranes regulate transport.

flashcards.question: Do prokaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus?
flashcards.answer: No. Their DNA is not enclosed in a membrane-bound nucleus.

flashcards.question: What is the role of the large central vacuole in plant cells?
flashcards.answer: Storage and support through maintenance of turgor pressure.

quiz.question: Which structure synthesizes proteins?
quiz.explanation: Ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis.

quiz.question: Which structure regulates movement across the cell boundary?
quiz.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.

quiz.question: Where does photosynthesis occur in plant cells?
quiz.explanation: Chloroplasts are the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.

quiz.question: Which organelle is involved in aerobic ATP production?
quiz.explanation: Mitochondria are involved in aerobic cellular respiration.

quiz.question: What distinguishes prokaryotic cells from eukaryotic cells?
quiz.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

identification.question: Identify the structure that synthesizes proteins.
Identify the organelle involved in photosynthesis.

true_false.statement: Prokaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
true_false.explanation: They do not have a membrane-bound nucleus.

true_false.statement: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.
true_false.explanation: It regulates which substances cross the cell boundary.

key_terms.definition: The basic structural and functional unit of living organisms.
A selectively permeable boundary that regulates movement into and out of a cell.
An organelle that contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s DNA.
An organelle involved in aerobic cellular respiration and ATP production.
The organelle where photosynthesis occurs in plant cells.

learning_objectives: Match each organelle to its main function.
common_misconceptions: A cell wall and a cell membrane are not the same structure.
examples: Ribosomes make proteins; chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
review_questions: What distinguishes prokaryotic and eukaryotic organization?
How do the cell wall and central vacuole contribute to support?
study_guide.final_summary: Practice retrieving the function of each structure, then explain how those functions support the cell.
